observations: Four photos show black salon chairs with chrome bases and armrests, arranged in a yard or workshop.
The chairs have black upholstery, some showing wear and scuffs, especially on the seat and armrests.
The base is a circular chrome pedestal with a footrest, typical of salon chairs.
Photo 2 shows a close-up of one chair with a headrest and a chrome armrest with a cutout design.
Photo 3 shows a side view of a chair with a chrome armrest and a footrest attached to the base.
The chairs appear to be in a used condition, with visible dirt and minor damage on the upholstery.
No brand or model is visible on any chair in any photo.
The seller claims 'Executive Salon chairs every part fully functional' and 'Like new, never repaired or opened, works perfectly. Original receipt and warranty available.'

claims.claim: Executive Salon chairs every part fully functional
claims.evidence: Photos show the chairs' structure and base, but no proof of functionality (e.g., height adjustment, tilt, or recline) is visible. No video or demonstration is provided.

claims.claim: Like new, never repaired or opened, works perfectly. Original receipt and warranty available.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: Chairs may not be fully functional (e.g., height adjustment, tilt, or recline mechanisms may be broken or missing)
risks.proof: A video showing the chair being adjusted in height, tilted, and reclined, or a close-up of the adjustment levers and mechanisms.

risks.risk: Upholstery may be damaged or worn beyond repair, especially on the seat and armrests
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the seat and armrests showing the extent of wear and tear.
risks.if_unproven: priced as used with visible wear

risks.risk: Base or pedestal may be unstable or have rusted joints, posing safety risks
risks.proof: Close-up of the base joints, legs, and pedestal for signs of rust, cracks, or loose connections.

proof_requests: Video showing the chair being adjusted in height, tilted, and reclined.
Close-up photos of the seat and armrests to assess upholstery condition.
Close-up of the base and pedestal joints to check for rust or damage.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
